thread:
Lina: morning — heads up: shared-gpu pool saturated around 07:15 UTC, p99 gen latency jumped to ~1.8s and queue depth tripled. tracing points to tenant:unit-42 sending repeated mini-bursts.
Ashok: saw the spike. unit-42 again? they were noisy last week too.
Mike: confirmed. arrival pattern is bursty (10–30 RPS bursts for ~60s) with long sequence lengths. Not a single huge job, more like rapid small requests that build queue.
Lara (ops-bot): (automated) ALERT: shared-pool-queue-depth > 500 for 6m in us-west-2 :warning:
Tara: current fairshare is flat-per-tenant. that makes bursts win the short game. we need admission that smooths across minutes, not just seconds.
Chen: sketching an approach: per-tenant soft token-bucket + short reservoir that can absorb occasional bursts + global capacity-aware cap. rough pseudocode:
```
# per-tenant
allow = token_bucket.consume(1)
if not allow:
  return 429, Retry-After
# global
if global_queue_len > Q_max_soft:
  throttle_top_k_consumers()
```
Also reservoir decays: credit = max(0, credit - decay * elapsed) so credits can't accumulate forever.
Mike: agree with decay. also track "recent-burstiness" metric to identify repetitive offenders.
Ashok: weighting: R_t should be base_rate * tier_multiplier * fairness_score. reserved customers keep guaranteed headroom.
Tara: routing option: when a region is saturated, we can optionally route to same-model in another region if SLA allows. need product & cost signoff — cross-region egress and latency tradeoffs.
Lina: ops needs: dashboards for per-tenant 429/s, token deficit, p50/p95/p99, queue wait time, eviction count, and reroute rate. we should annotate traces with admission decisions.
Chen: will add trace attrs: admission.bucket_rate, admission.tokens_left, admission.decision, admission.reason. makes debugging postmortems easier.
Mike: rollout plan: feature flag admission logic, canary 5% on a subset of shared nodes (us-west-2), monitor 48h + prompt-set regressions, then 50% then global. include kill switch for immediate rollback.
Tara: cost note reiterated: reroute increases egress costs; include cost estimator in RFC and limit reroute by budget.
Ashok: soft 429 + Retry-After header preferred. escalate to hard evict only after repeated offenses (e.g., >X 429s in Y minutes). also run a daily job to recompute tenant weights from 7d usage + error history.
Lina: I'll author RFC PR with configs, metric names, and a sample playbook for canary/revert. will include dashboard mockups. please +1 or add comments.
Mike: +1
Chen: +1 — prefer exponential Retry-After guidance and clear logs for decisions.
Tara: +1 pending cost appendix on reroute
Ashok: +1. add alerting for "unexpected drop in p50 for tiered tenants" so we catch regressions quickly.
Lina: thanks team. I'll tag @ops-bot to follow up when RFC lands and schedule a short review session.
